title: Reducedness, finite singular locus and adjunction presentations of a nodal curve
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $p:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a finite-type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $C$ pure of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Assume that every point where $p$ is not smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is closed and has maximal-ideal-adic completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] isomorphic as a $k$-algebra to $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Neither separatedness nor properness is assumed.
Then $C$ is Noetherian (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]) and reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The morphism $p$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]); all its nonempty geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are pure of dimension $1$. It has an affine open cover by local complete intersections over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field], with closed-immersion presentations [def-weil-closed-immersion] into opens of affine $n$-space whose defining ideals are locally generated by regular sequences of length $n-1$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The closed subscheme $T$ cut out by the first Fitting ideal of the relative differentials [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme] is a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$; its support is exactly the nonsmooth locus. Consequently the smooth locus contains every generic point [def-sc-generic-point]. The adjunction construction of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction] applies with $d=1$, and its invertible module $K_{C/k}$ [def-sc-invertible-module] has the canonical identification $K_{C/k}|_{C_{\mathrm{sm}}}\cong\Omega^1_{C_{\mathrm{sm}}/k}$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf].

source.place: Tags 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci) and 0E37 (lemma-facts-about-nodal-curves); adjunction consequence via lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction. Agent synthesis of these inputs, not a verbatim Stacks statement.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, so its spectrum is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $p$ to obtain that $C$ is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. By [lem-pc-flat-field], $p$ is flat. By [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth], it is locally of finite presentation. It is quasi-compact by finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], $C$ is quasi-separated; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) then makes $p$ quasi-separated. These are exactly the three conditions for finite presentation in the statement.

Use $k$ itself as its algebraic closure. Every closed point of $C$ is either smooth or satisfies precisely the completed geometric local-ring condition in [lem-trf-nodal-curve-lci-criterion](1). That criterion gives an affine open cover by finitely generated local-complete-intersection $k$-algebras and makes $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ unramified. Independently, [lem-trf-nodal-points-reduced-algebraically-closed] applies to these same closed points and proves that $C$ is reduced. Neither cited statement assumes separatedness or properness.

source.place: Tags 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci), implication (1) to (2), and 0E37 (lemma-facts-about-nodal-curves), reducedness paragraph.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-field-curve-fitting-smooth-preparation], the support of $T$ is exactly the nonsmooth locus. Apply [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition] to the unramified morphism of step 2: $T$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions $L_i/k$. Each is $k$: the minimal polynomial of any element of $L_i$ is irreducible over the algebraically closed field $k$, hence linear. This union is finite. Indeed $|T|$ is closed in the quasi-compact $|C|$; an open cover of $|T|$, lifted to opens of $|C|$ and augmented by $|C|\setminus|T|$, has a finite subcover. Thus $|T|$ is quasi-compact, and its disjoint singleton open cover has a finite subcover. This proves the scheme-theoretic assertion, including the absence of nilpotent thickening at singular points.

If a generic point of an irreducible component were nonsmooth, it would be closed by hypothesis. Its closure would then be a singleton and also the whole component, which would have dimension $0$, contradicting pure dimension $1$. Thus every generic point is smooth. This is vacuous when $C$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci), dense smooth open assertion, here obtained directly from the stated closedness hypothesis.

proof.text: The sole ordinary fibre of $p$ is $C$, pure of dimension $1$. Apply [lem-trf-relative-dimension-base-change] to $p$ with $d=1$. For every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, the base-changed structure morphism has its sole nonempty fibre pure of dimension $1$. This fibre is exactly $C_\Omega$, so this supplies all geometric fibre hypotheses of adjunction; it does not identify the underlying spaces of $C$ and $C_\Omega$.

Fix $x\in C$. From the lci cover in step 2 and [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion](1)$\Rightarrow$(2), choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with a global complete intersection presentation $B=Q/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$, $Q=k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, $B\ne0$, and $\dim B=n-c$. By [lem-trf-locally-algebraic-dimension-components], pure dimension $1$ gives $\dim_x C=1$. The opens containing $x$ inside $U$ are cofinal among its neighbourhoods in $C$, so $\dim_x U=1$ as well. By [lem-weil-pbc-global-complete-intersection-equidimensional], $\dim_x U=n-c$. Therefore $c=n-1$.

source.place: Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field), the following equidimensionality paragraph; varieties.tex Tags 0A21 and 0B1B (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic, component formula).

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q\subset Q$ be the inverse image of the prime of $x$ in the presentation of step 6. By [lem-weil-pbc-global-complete-intersection-local-regular-sequence], the $f_i$ form a regular sequence in $Q_{\mathfrak q}$. The polynomial ring $Q$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], applied over the Noetherian field $k$. Hence [lem-exc-regular-sequence-principal-neighbourhood] gives $h\notin\mathfrak q$ such that the same ordered equations are regular in $Q_h$. The quotient is $Q_h/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)=B_{\bar h}$, by sending each fraction to the fraction of its residue class. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}B_{\bar h}$ is an affine neighbourhood of $x$, and $\operatorname{Spec}Q_h$ is an open of $\mathbf A^n_k$. The quotient gives the desired closed immersion, defined by a regular sequence of length $c=n-1$. Repeating at every point gives the cover.

source.place: Tags 00SB (lemma-lci-CM) and 00SC (lemma-lci), regular equations at primes; 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 061L (lemma-regular-sequence-in-neighbourhood); schemes.tex Tag 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $W=C$ and $d=1$. Its base is Noetherian, step 1 gives flat finite presentation, step 5 gives pure one-dimensional nonempty geometric fibres, and step 7 gives precisely the regular presentations of codimension $n-d$. Its statement explicitly allows nonseparated $W/S$. It produces the invertible module $K_{C/k}$ with the canonical smooth-locus identification $K_{C/k}|_{C_{\mathrm{sm}}}\cong\Omega^1_{C_{\mathrm{sm}}/k}$. Here differentials are the affine-chart relative differential sheaf of [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], valid without separatedness, and the degree-one exterior power in adjunction is the module itself.

source.place: Tag 0B6V (lemma-lci-shriek), local regular-immersion computation; application of the nonseparated adjunction statement, not of a global separated shriek formalism.
